headline: Denmark's foreign minister says Trump's diesel deal must not undermine sanctions on Russia
deck: America has temporarily eased sanctions to let Russia sell diesel; Ukraine's president says the deal gives Moscow more money for war.
standard: Lars Løkke Rasmussen, the foreign minister, said on Saturday that the EU's work on sanctions against Russia 'must not be undermined' by a diesel deal between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin. Extra income for Russia could in the end pay for the war in Ukraine, he told DR.

Under the deal, Trump says, Russia will at once deliver 300,000 tonnes of diesel to the American and global market. The US Treasury has given temporary permission for sanctions to be eased so that Russia can sell diesel internationally, until 7 April 2027 according to Reuters.
Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukraine's president, wrote on Friday that the deal would give Russia more money to wage war.
short: Lars Løkke Rasmussen, the foreign minister, said on Saturday that the EU's work on sanctions against Russia 'must not be undermined' by Donald Trump's diesel deal with Vladimir Putin, which America has backed by temporarily easing sanctions on Russian diesel.
